description: A litigation director must approve whether the firm will file an amicus brief in a pending appellate matter and finalize the brief's permitted argument, client references, and conflict safeguards, with input from appellate counsel, the client liaison, and conflicts counsel.

shared_context.S1: The state supreme court is considering an amicus brief in a case affecting the enforceability of software-service arbitration clauses.
shared_context.S2: The court's filing window closes this Friday, and the litigation director has final approval authority for the firm's filing.
shared_context.S3: The draft brief currently supports enforceability, identifies the firm's client as a software provider, and contains no conflict-screening terms.
shared_context.S4: The firm's weekly filing review requires the litigation director to ask appellate, client, and conflicts personnel for relevant information before approving an amicus filing.

PF1.text: While checking the court's current online filing materials this morning, Tom found a standing order limiting amicus briefs in this case to the certified question of whether the arbitration clause was incorporated by reference and to exactly 12 pages; he has not yet circulated the standing order to the filing team.

PF2.text: During yesterday's call, the client instructed Nia that the brief must not identify the client by name or include examples that would identify its products; Nia has not put that instruction into the draft comments yet.

PF3.text: Greg's completed conflicts-database review found that the firm's litigation group represented the opposing party's parent in an unrelated matter two years ago, so filing requires the client's informed written consent and an ethical screen separating the amicus team from that former-matter team; he was waiting for the matter-number confirmation before adding this to the approval checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The firm must file the amicus brief.
The brief must support enforceability only on the certified question of incorporation by reference.
The brief must be exactly 12 pages or fewer.
The client must not be identified by name.
The brief must contain no identifying product examples.
Informed written client consent must be required before filing.
An ethical screen must be required before filing.
The standing-order finding must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C3: 'incorporation by reference' in decisions['argument_scope'] and decisions['page_limit'] == 12
content_checks.C9: decisions['written_consent_required'] == True and decisions['ethical_screen_required'] == True and any('ethical screen' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The standing order changes the ordinary broad enforceability brief to the exact incorporation-by-reference-only scope and the exact 12-page limit.
The client's instruction changes the filing from naming the client with product examples to omitting both the client name and identifying product examples.
The prior representation changes the filing package from having no safeguards to requiring informed written consent and an ethical screen, including an explicit ethical-screen commitment.
